# CLI Anything InkStitch

Curated by Skill Harbor — the agent-facing operating manual for `cli-anything-inkstitch`, a stateful command-line interface for machine-embroidery digitization: it writes `inkstitch:` attributes onto SVG elements, then delegates stitch math to the Ink/Stitch binary. Covers document/element/params/commands/tools/validate/preview/export/schema/session/font/artifact command groups with examples — including digitize-lineart (raster → verified stroke design), stitch-sim QA rendering of DST files, density maps, font import/composition, and an undo/checkpoint system — plus 22 hard-won operating rules for AI agents (always use --json, describe before assigning params, validate before export, stitch-sim after every export). Pairs with the embroidery-digitization skill for the decision wisdom. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @bobbymarko. Honest caveats: requires Python 3.10+, `pip install cli-anything-inkstitch`, and the Ink/Stitch binary installed and on PATH (free) — the agent drives a real tool on your machine; review commands before bulk runs. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
